reason: The text (Numbers 13-14 in Hebrew) is centrally focused on Moses as a leader dealing with the Israelites' ingratitude and rebellion. The narrative highlights Moses's actions in sending the spies, his efforts to intercede with God, and the people's complaints directed at him and Aaron. Key evidence includes the people's laments (wishing they had died in Egypt, wanting to return, questioning why God brought them), their explicit complaints against Moses and Aaron ('וַיִּלֹּנוּ עַל־ מֹשֶׁה וְעַֽל־ אַהֲרֹן'), and their proposal to choose a new leader and return to Egypt. Throughout, Moses is portrayed as the focal point responding to their ingratitude, though the narrative is presented in third-person rather than Moses's subjective first-person perspective.
